newsitem.title: USA: Norcen sees doubling Venezuela oil output.
newsitem.headline: Norcen sees doubling Venezuela oil output.

text.p: Canada's Norcen Energy Resources Ltd expects to double its oil output from the Oritupano-Leona block in northern Venezuela over the next two to four years, Norcen president and chief executive Grant Billing said on Thursday.

The block, in which Norcen acquired a 45 percent working interest in 1994, should be producing 30,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day net to Norcen in that time, Billing told an investment symposium.
Norcen's current output from Oritupano-Leona is about 15,000 barrels per day, he said, adding the company expects reserves in the block to total several hundred millions of barrels.

The block is "mainly what you might call exploration and development as most of it is reactivating and infill drilling", Billing told Reuters. "But we've started doing exploration work around the block for new reservoirs and new pools as well and have been successful in finding two new pools this year."
Billing said Norcen's estimated 1996 expenditure on the block, where wells average production of 500 to 700 barrels per day, is C$60 million.
Norcen recovers its capital spending on the project on a fee-for-service basis with interest. It is also paid US$5.25 per barrel to cover operating costs.

The company also has a 35 percent working interest in Venezuela's Delta Centro exploration block, bought at the country's January 1996 bidding round. Louisiana Land and Exploration Co is the operator of the project.
In this project Norcen pays a more traditional royalty and is subject to a 30-percent cash tax, Billing said.
The block has no current production and the partners are expected to drill an exploration well late next year, he said.
Billing said Norcen, which also operates in Canada and the Gulf of Mexico, has begun to concentrate on growth in its core areas after selling about C$1.2 billion of assets over the past two years.
At present Norcen produces about 10 percent of its total output in Venezuela.
